correctness.rationale: The proof explicitly constructs one analytic Banach space with no regularity loss: Fourier decimation gives a norm-convergent inverse on the fibrewise zero-mean subspace, inverse branch holomorphy on a wider strip makes the perturbed STO jointly holomorphic into the original space, and the analytic implicit function theorem constructs the stationary density. Mass and reality/positivity are justified, the formal-coefficient recursion agrees term by term, and Cauchy estimates prove convergence and remainder. Exact two-block Fourier equations were executed as checks. Limits: local solution only, and symbolic tests do not prove all-order claims.

originality.rationale: Maquera 2026 Proposition 3.11 explicitly limits genuine susceptibility coefficients to orders one and two and leaves both genuineness at higher orders and convergence open. This claim proves holomorphic all-order response in the integer-affine, analytic finite-harmonic subclass with bounded graphons. Exact claim comparisons with the published formal tree theorem, homogeneous linear response, analytic ordinary Perron operators and relevant prior records found no dominating result; priority is provisional.

value.rationale: Maquera 2026 explicitly isolates the nontrivial distinction between all-order formally defined graphon-tree susceptibilities and genuine convergent equilibrium response. The present result resolves both questions simultaneously on a natural analytic subclass while allowing arbitrary measurable graphons, and provides finite-truncation error bounds in a graphon-uniform analytic norm; the first two known coefficients are used only as reproducibility checks.
